newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian economy remains subdued - survey.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian economy remains subdued - survey.

text.p: The Australian economy is still underperforming with business conditions and confidence continuing to fall, according a survey released on Sunday.
The Australian Chamber of Commerce and Industry (ACCI) said its index of investor confidence fell to 41.1 in December from 41.4 in July and 44.7 in the previous corresponding period.
It said an index level below 50 indicated business conditions were unsatisfactory.
More than half of the 140 companies surveyed described current economic conditions as poor or very poor, it said.
"There should be little doubt that the economy remains deeply constrained," the ACCI said in a statement. "The economy has slowed and business remains wary and tentative."
It said the most encouraging sign was a change in sentiment regarding interest rates with most businesses now expecting interest rates to fall.
"(This) will assist in the process of recovery," the ACCI said. "But the figures also show that the fall in interest rates was a long time overdue, given how subdued the level of activity was."
The ACCI said its survey showed that there was a greater need than ever before for the government to return its budget to surplus.
It called for the government to direct more of its spending towards infrastructure and capital, and said the taxation system needed to be overhauled.
"Tax reform remains the number one priority with the business community," it said.
The survey found profitability was particularly subdued with 44.8 percent of the respondents describing conditions as poor, very poor or deeply depressed.
Private investment and employment growth were also expected to remain subdued, although activity levels were seen rising.
Australian GDP grew 0.8 percent in the September quarter, to stand 3.8 percent higher than a year before.
The Reserve Bank of Australia eased monetary policy in July, November and December, citing subdued inflationary pressure.
